auth.loginSubtitle: Sign in to see your wealth and dividend data.
auth.invalidCredentials: That username and password did not match.
auth.signInFailed: Sign-in is unavailable right now. Please try again in a moment.
auth.sessionExpired: Your session has expired. Please sign in again.

import.downloadDataHint: Every row you own, in the same format - keep it as a backup, edit it in a spreadsheet and upload it again, or take it to another account.
import.notCsv: That is not a CSV file. Choose a file whose name ends in .csv.
import.duplicates: {{count}} rows were already stored and were skipped.
import.failed: {{count}} rows could not be read and were skipped.

rates.title: Import / export exchange rates
rates.hint: Fill the sample in and upload it to store a whole file of quotes at once. Commas and semicolons both work as separators. A row for a pair and date you already quoted replaces that quote.

dividends.title: Import / export dividends
dividends.hint: Fill the sample in and upload it to record a whole file of payments at once. Commas and semicolons both work as separators. Name the company by its ticker symbol; rows you have already recorded are skipped, so an overlapping file is safe to upload.

expenseItems.title: Import / export expenses
expenseItems.hint: Fill the sample in and upload it to record a whole file of recurring costs at once. name, amount, unit and period are required; interval defaults to 1, both dates may be blank, and categories is a '|'-separated list in one cell. A category named there is created for you if you do not have it yet. Rows whose name you already have are skipped.

expenseCategories.title: Import / export categories
expenseCategories.hint: One name per line, under a 'category' header. Names you already have - or that exist as global categories - are skipped, so an overlapping list is safe to upload.

instruments.title: Import / export instruments
instruments.hint: Fill the sample in and upload it to add or update a whole list of instruments at once. Rows are matched on ticker symbol: a symbol you already have is updated from its row, a new one is created. symbol, name, currency and assetType are required; exchange, sector and active may be left out, and a blank active keeps the instrument's current status. Commas and semicolons both work as separators.
instruments.downloadDataHint: The whole instrument list in the same format - edit it in a spreadsheet and upload it again to apply the changes. Unchanged rows are reported as already stored.

inflation.title: Import / export inflation
inflation.hint: Fill the sample in and upload it to store a whole file of figures at once. unit, year and rate are required; rate is in percent and may end in %. A row for a currency and year that is already stored replaces that figure. Commas and semicolons both work as separators.
inflation.downloadDataHint: Every stored figure in the same format - edit it in a spreadsheet and upload it again to apply the changes. Unchanged rows are reported as already stored.

home.title: Stock Market Analyzer
home.subtitle: Market data and a personal net-worth ledger in one place.
home.wealthBlurb: Record what you hold, in which unit, on which date - and see it valued from your own exchange rates.
home.signedOutBlurb: Wealth data is private to your account. Sign in to see and edit it.

wealth.noRate: No exchange rate connects these units on this date.

form.quantityHint: Leave empty for an aggregate row that only sums the entries under it.

entries.title: Wealth entries
entries.cloneHint: Every copied row takes the date above. Leave a quantity empty to make that row an aggregate, and a unit empty to inherit the one above it.
entries.cascadeMessage: "{{name}}" has entries rolling up into it. Delete the whole subtree?

wealth.partialValue: Something under this row has no exchange rate, so the total is a lower bound.
wealth.mixedUnits: This row mixes units, so quantities cannot be added. The value still rolls up.

rates.title: Exchange rates
rates.hint: Your own conversion factors plus the global ones shared by everybody. Entries are valued from the newest rate on or before their own date - and where you have quoted a pair yourself, your rate always wins over the global one.
rates.fetchHint: Reads the configured pairs from the central bank feed and stores each one as a global rate for everybody, under the date it was published — on a weekend, the previous working day.
rates.deleteMessage: Delete the {{source}} to {{destination}} rate quoted on {{date}}?
rates.globalHint: A global rate is used for every user who has not quoted that pair themselves. A personal rate always wins.
rates.kindFixedHint: A rate cannot be moved between personal and global. Store the other kind as a new rate instead.

dividends.title: Received dividends
dividends.hint: What you were actually paid, and when. Each row is valued from your own exchange rates using the rate in force on its payment date.
dividends.partialTotal: Some matching rows have no exchange rate, so the total is a lower bound.

form.noInstruments: No instruments are set up yet - an administrator has to add them first.
form.unitHint: What actually landed in the account, which need not be what the instrument trades in.

monthly.title: Dividends by month
monthly.hint: Every payment in the range, laid out by calendar month. Hover a figure for the other currency and the payments behind it.
monthly.empty: Nothing was paid in this range.
monthly.chartNote: Months are totalled in {{unit}}, using the rate in force on each payment date - the only way currencies can be added up.
monthly.chartNoteFiltered: Filtered to {{unit}}, so the bars are the amounts as received and no exchange rate is involved.
monthly.inflationNote: Each figure is multiplied by the cumulative inflation from its payment year through the latest year with data ({{years}}). Amounts use the inflation of the currency they were received in; converted values are converted at the payment date's rate first, then adjusted with {{valueUnit}} inflation.
monthly.inflationMissing: No inflation data covers {{units}}, so {{count}} figures are shown unadjusted.

dividends.inflationNote: Amounts are multiplied by the cumulative inflation of their own currency from the payment year through the latest year with data; values are converted at the payment date's rate first, then adjusted with {{valueUnit}} inflation. Sorting and the total use the adjusted figures. Hover a figure for the original.
dividends.notInflationAdjusted: No inflation data covers this payment's year for one of its currencies, so a figure is shown unadjusted.
dividends.notInflationAdjustedTotal: {{count}} payments could not be fully adjusted for want of inflation data.

totals.rateHint: Converted with the most recent rate stored for each pair.
totals.partial: Some rows have no exchange rate, so the total is a lower bound.
totals.note: {{counted}} of {{total}} rows counted - only what is being charged now.

expenses.noRate: No stored exchange rate connects these units.

view.label: View
view.groupedNote: Categories are tags, so an expense carrying two of them is listed - and counted - under both. The total above the table counts every expense once.

form.recurrenceHint: Pick Custom... for anything this list does not cover, such as every 7 weeks.
form.startHint: Optional. Leave it empty if this is simply what you pay.
form.expiryHint: Optional. A loan ends; a subscription usually does not.
form.noCategories: No categories yet - add some on the Categories screen.
form.datesWrongWay: The expiry date is before the start date.

items.title: Regular expenses
items.hint: What comes back, how much it is and how often. The totals are worked out here, per currency, from the amount and the recurrence - nothing is converted between currencies.

chart.title: Expenses by share
chart.note: {{counted}} expenses, per {{period}}, in {{unit}}. Slices under 1% are summed into Other.
chart.empty: Nothing to chart: every expense here is worth zero.
chart.pickCurrency: Pick a currency above. A pie needs one whole, and amounts in different currencies cannot share one.

categories.title: Expense categories
categories.hint: Tags for your expenses. The global ones are shared by everybody and only an administrator can change them.
categories.globalHint: A global category is offered to every user of this installation.
categories.kindFixedHint: Personal and global cannot be swapped: one would hand your label to everybody, the other would take a shared one away from them.

users.title: Users
users.hint: The accounts that can sign in to Stock Market Analyzer. Created, reset and granted privileges here — there is no separate identity console to visit.
users.conflict: That username or email address is already taken
users.disableMessage: Disable "{{username}}"? They will not be able to sign in, and everything recorded under the account is kept.
users.resetHint: The old password is not needed. Pass the new one on yourself — nothing is emailed.
users.notYourself: You cannot do this to your own account
users.notYourAdmin: You cannot take the ADMIN role away from yourself. Ask another administrator to do it.
users.passwordHint: At least {{min}} characters. The realm's own password policy still applies.
users.temporaryHint: A temporary password must be changed at the next sign-in, so the one you type here stops working as soon as it has been used once.

instruments.title: Instruments
instruments.hint: The reference list of tradable instruments that every picker in the application offers. An inactive instrument disappears from the pickers but keeps its history.
instruments.renameHint: Renaming the ticker keeps the instrument's dividends and price history attached.
instruments.activeHint: Only active instruments are offered in pickers, such as the one on the dividends page.
instruments.deleteMessage: Delete {{symbol}} together with its price history? This cannot be undone.
instruments.inUseMessage: Dividends have been recorded against {{symbol}}, so it cannot be deleted. Deactivate it instead? It disappears from the pickers and the recorded history stays.

inflation.title: Inflation
inflation.hint: Annual inflation per currency, in percent: 4.6 means 4.6%, and a negative figure is deflation. The figures are annual average HICP rates; Fetch reads them from Eurostat (HUF: Hungary, EUR: the euro area, USD: the United States, which Eurostat publishes about a year later). They are shared by every user.
inflation.empty: No inflation figures match the filters.
inflation.conflict: That currency and year already have a figure
inflation.newHint: If the currency already has a figure for that year, it is replaced.
inflation.editHint: The currency and the year can be corrected too, as long as no other row holds them.
inflation.deleteMessage: Delete the {{unit}} inflation figure for {{year}}? This cannot be undone.
inflation.fetchHint: Reads HUF, EUR and USD from Eurostat and stores only the years after the latest one already stored for each currency - every published year for a currency that has none. Stored figures are never overwritten.
